To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have introduced frame-based CNNs, that can be steered dynamically, that are more expressive than the traditional pixel basis.
Frame-based convolutional neural networks and Dynamic Steirable Frame Networks allow to continuously transform features and data-efficiently learn to recognize objects in different poses.

we present a novel approach for convolutional neural networks that is able to learn to transform its features and data in a continuous manner, and that we show the advantages of this approach in terms of error rates on the Cifar-10 dataset, edge detection and hand-gesture recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generalization of convolutional networks and their dynamic regularization.
the generalization of CNNs by extending the pixel basis with steerable frames.

the general question of how we can extend the set of possible filter bases for convolutional layers in order to achieve improved performance on image classification and hand-gesture recognition tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed steerable frames and the derived Dynamic Steerable Frame network are a promising approach for pose-invariant feature learning.
we have demonstrated that frames can improve convolutional networks and we have demonstrated a novel way of transforming features and data.
we have presented a novel method for dynamic transformation of features in convolutional networks, that allows for data-efficient learning of pose invariant appearance features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generalized convolutional neural networks to a more general basis and shown advantages of this generalization in the context of dynamic transformations.

we have shown a novel method to dynamically transform CNN filters conditioned on their input and that this method can be applied to any CNN architecture, as we have illustrated with the examples of a dynamic steerable filter network for edge detection and a steerable frame convolutional LSTM for hand-gesture recognition.
we have shown that frames provide a more expressive basis for CNN filters than the pixel basis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
frames are a viable alternative to pixel bases for convolutional networks and that steerable frames can be exploited to continuously transform features and regularize the training.
we have extended the set of viable convolutional bases from orthonormal bases to generalized frames and derived a method for learning continuous transformations in CNNs.

frame bases allow to continuously transform filters and data under arbitrary Lie-groups, which we illustrate with Dynamic Steerable Frame networks that dynamically estimate such transformations conditioned on the input.
